blocks.md:
- A **Brønsted-Lowry acid **is a species that can donate a proton
- A **Brønsted-Lowry base **is a species that can accept a proton
- In an equilibrium reaction, the products are formed at the same rate as the reactants are used
acid                 base                    conjugate base             conjugate acid

- The reactant CH<sub>3</sub>COOH is linked to the product CH<sub>3</sub>COO<sup>- </sup>by the transfer of a **proton **from the acid to the base

  - Similarly, the H<sub>2</sub>O molecule is linked to H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> ion by the transfer of a proton
- These pairs are therefore called **conjugate acid-base pairs**

  - A **conjugate acid-base pair** is two species that are different from each other by a H<sup>+</sup> ion
  
    - **Conjugate **here means related
    - In other words, the acid and base are related to each other by one proton difference

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
**Identifying conjugate acid-base pairs**

Identify the conjugate acid-base pairs in the following equilibrium reaction:

**NH**<sub>**3**</sub>** (g) + H**<sub>**2**</sub>**O (l) **$\rightleftharpoons$** NH**<sub>**4**</sub><sup>**+**</sup>** (aq) + OH**<sup>**–**</sup>** (aq)**

**Answer:**

- In the forward reaction:

  - NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> is the conjugate acid of the base NH<sub>3</sub>
  - OH<sup>-</sup> is the conjugate base of the acid H<sub>2</sub>O
- In the reverse reaction

  - NH<sub>3</sub> is the conjugate base of the acid NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>
  - H<sub>2</sub>O is the conjugate acid of the base OH<sup>–</sup>

blocks.md:
In the equilibrium reaction shown below, which species are a conjugate acid-base pair?

**CH**<sub>**3**</sub>**CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**COOH (aq)  +  H**<sub>**2**</sub>**O (l) ⇌ CH**<sub>**3**</sub>**CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**COO**<sup>**- **</sup>**(aq)  +  H**<sub>**3**</sub>**O**<sup>**+**</sup>** (aq) **

**   A**.    CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH and H<sub>2</sub>O

**   B**.    H<sub>2</sub>O and H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>

**   C**.    H<sub>2</sub>O and CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COO<sup>-</sup>

**   D**.   CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COO<sup>- </sup>and H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>

**Answer:**

- The correct option in **B**

  - A conjugate acid-base pair differ only by an H<sup>+</sup> ion
